description: Spec Kit and Superpowers Bridge are installed and readable from the repository.
The doctor command reports storage, provider, harness, and workflow readiness in text and JSON modes.
The repository can sync upcoming fixtures from API-Football for the configured leagues into shared storage.
The fixtures command reads upcoming fixtures from the shared cache and still supports a demo fallback.
DuckDB is initialized as the shared objective-data cache for fixtures.
SQLite stores mutable sync-run metadata and the latest run can be inspected in doctor output.
CLI operations can emit LangSmith traces when enabled and configured.
The repository can load a cached fixture and build a structured snapshot with FBref season metrics plus Understat recent-form and shot-summary data.
The snapshot now includes market value, injuries, and confirmed-or-probable lineups with explicit source attribution.
Shared DuckDB reference data can reconcile provider player aliases and persist venue/weather cache support.
A local-first materialization layer exists for Transfermarkt and soccerdata inputs used by the fixture snapshot.
The fixture snapshot now renders environment, deeper availability, and matchup/trend context with truthful unavailable markers.
The repository can build a fixture-linked odds snapshot with canonical markets, fair probabilities, and historical market drift summaries.
The odds path can reconcile a cached fixture into a The Odds API event, cache that link, and normalize the secondary provider behind the same contract.
The repository contains init, progress, and feature-list artifacts for long-running agent continuity.
Continuous integration runs lint and tests for the Sprint 0 foundation.
The repository can synthesize fixture snapshot and odds snapshot context into a four-part pre-match judgment through a dedicated CLI workflow.
The repository can generate local graph-native architecture assets with make graph and graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md.
The Odds API provider health metrics persist in DuckDB and agent-status can report them without network calls.
The CLI can produce a single operator-facing pre-match brief that packages agent status, deterministic judgment, evidence, caveats, and optional generated synthesis.
A no-network IM bot adapter can parse /brief messages, reuse the match brief workflow, and run through nutmeg bot-dry-run.
The CLI can list today/local fixture candidates and optionally fan out match briefs without manually entering fixture ids.
A Telegram Bot API transport can poll one update batch, owner-gate chat ids, and route allowed messages through the existing bot adapter.
Telegram bot can run a controlled polling daemon loop with offset tracking, owner gating, graceful interruption, and aggregate summaries.
The CLI can rank local/demo fixture candidates by deterministic popularity, explain scores, and reuse the ranking inside today-briefs.
BotAdapter can answer /start/help deterministically and optionally route unsupported or failed bot messages through an OpenAI Responses API GPT-5.5 fallback without leaking secrets.
Telegram polling stores next_offset locally and resumes from it by default, eliminating manual offset tracking across restarts.
The CLI can rank model-vs-market match-winner value candidates with baseline Poisson/Dixon-Coles-lite probabilities, fair-probability edge, and quarter-Kelly sizing.
The CLI can build a local-first player profile with identity, Transfermarkt market data, cached season metrics, availability status, and similar-player scoring.
The repository can run local eval datasets and record/review match-winner predictions with Brier Score calibration.
The CLI can run a safe daily operator cycle over optional fixture sync, popular matches, value board, optional briefs, and explicit Telegram dispatch.
The CLI can generate deterministic local SVG shot-map, lineup-network, and xG-trend artifacts from fixture snapshot context while labeling proxy/missing sections truthfully.
The CLI can load local StatsBomb-like event data, build pass-network, xT-lite, and VAEP-lite tactical reports, and emit deterministic SVG artifacts without network calls.

Nutmeg can build local-first source-attributed fixture information digests from JSON/RSS files, expose them through fixture-information, and render reliability-labeled updates in the AI-native match workspace.

Nutmeg can use explicit information source manifests with opt-in HTTP/RSS/JSON fetching, local cache reads, stale fallback warnings, and client-match manifest overrides without scraping or default network calls.

Nutmeg exposes a Chinese-first Web/PWA client plus JSON CLI parity for daily betting-analysis triage, match workspaces, grounded follow-up, subscription-ready user isolation, alerts, and calibration records.
